title: Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium Land Transfer Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on October 22, 2013. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium Land Transfer Act - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to convey by warranty deed to the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC) specified property in Anchorage, Alaska, for use in connection with health and related programs.

Requires the property to be conveyed without requiring any consideration from, or imposing any obligations, terms, or conditions on, the ANTHC.

Describes the property as Tract A-3A, Tudor Centre, according to plat number 2013-43, recorded on June 20, 2013 in Anchorage recording district, Alaska.

Absolves the ANTHC from liability for any environmental contamination or hazard on the property on or before the date on which the property was conveyed by quitclaim deed.

summary.headline: Directs the federal health agency to transfer a specific Anchorage, Alaska property to the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium for health programs.
summary.what_it_does: The law tells the Secretary of Health and Human Services to give a described piece of land in Anchorage, Alaska, to the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC). The land is described as Tract A-3A in the Tudor Centre subdivision, and the transfer is for use in health and related programs. The consortium does not have to pay for the land or accept any extra conditions. The summary says the transfer is made by warranty deed, but it later mentions a quitclaim deed when it releases the consortium from liability for environmental contamination on the property before the transfer.

who_it_affects.how: It receives ownership of the Anchorage property without paying for it or taking on listed obligations, and it is released from liability for pre-transfer environmental contamination.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Health and Human Services
who_it_affects.how: It must carry out the conveyance of the property to the consortium.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive health care from ANTHC programs
who_it_affects.how: The property is meant for use in connection with health and related programs, though the summary does not say which services would be offered there.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2013; the summary does not list a separate effective date or deadline for the transfer.
